executive_brief.title: Executive Brief

items.title: US–China strategic competition remains the primary geopolitical axis
items.fact: Export controls on advanced semiconductors and manufacturing equipment remain in force.
items.interpretation: This axis transmits into tech supply chains, capital allocation, and military posture; second-order effects dominate most other domains.

items.title: Advanced semiconductor manufacturing remains geographically concentrated
items.fact: Leading-edge logic capacity is highly concentrated in a small number of firms and locations.
items.interpretation: Concentration is a systemic risk node linking geopolitics, AI compute, and capital expenditure cycles.

items.title: Global policy rates remain elevated vs 2010s baseline
items.fact: Major advanced-economy policy rates are still well above the post-GFC low decade averages.
items.interpretation: Higher-for-longer or staggered cuts both reprice duration, risk assets, and the USD — critical for treasury liquidity and BTC beta.

items.title: Frontier AI remains compute- and energy-constrained
items.fact: Leading labs continue multi-billion-dollar training and inference buildouts.
items.interpretation: Personal leverage from AI tooling scales with model capability, but investable exposure is concentrated in semis, power, and platforms.

items.title: AI data-center load and grid constraints lift nuclear and firm power narratives
items.fact: Hyperscalers have announced long-dated power purchase interest including nuclear-linked supply.
items.interpretation: Energy scarcity becomes a binding constraint on AI scale-out; nuclear miners/utilities and grid equipment sit at the intersection of Energy and AI bets.

items.title: Bitcoin remains a high-beta expression of global liquidity and risk appetite
items.fact: Spot BTC ETFs and corporate treasury narratives have expanded institutional access channels.
items.interpretation: For a Bitcoin accumulation thesis, watch real rates, USD liquidity, ETF flows, and regulatory clarity as first-order drivers.

items.title: Advanced-economy aging and tight labor markets constrain growth potential
items.fact: Working-age population growth is slow or negative in several major economies.
items.interpretation: Demographics support structurally higher wage/inflation volatility and automation demand (AI/robotics leverage thesis).

executive_brief.note: Facts are listed separately from interpretation; confidence is explicit.
